subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicit `contents: read` access for the primary and fallback GitHub App tokens in both automated-response and label-routing workflows to satisfy the Workflow Sanity contract?
rationale: The patch intentionally broadens token access at a credential boundary; source-level correctness does not determine whether that extra repository visibility is acceptable for every trigger path.

options.title: Accept the scoped read grants
options.body: Confirm repository-content reads are required for both workflows, then rebase and merge after the exact merge result passes the workflow audit.

options.title: Narrow the token use first
options.body: Refactor the workflow or its configuration loading so the affected token paths do not need repository-content access before merging.

options.title: Pause for workflow ownership review
options.body: Keep the PR open until the owner of the GitHub App automation confirms the least-privilege contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped read grants
recommendation.body: Confirm repository-content reads are required for both workflows, then rebase and merge after the exact merge result passes the workflow audit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the permitted scope of repository automation credentials rather than the contributor's proposed implementation.
